To: d.kerrigan@northmail.example
Replying to: m01
Cc: none
Subject: Re: Blister packs for my mother - new patient

Dear Mr. Kerrigan,

Thank you for your email about your mother. I am the pharmacist at Erindale Park Pharmacy, and we would be glad to look after her medications. I am sorry to hear about her fall, and I hope she is recovering well.

To answer your questions:

1. Yes, we prepare weekly blister packs. Each pack covers 7 days, with up to four dosing times per day. There is no charge for the packaging itself. Your mother would pay only the normal dispensing fees, and at her age the Ontario Drug Benefit covers most of that.

2. We can deliver to her building. Delivery runs on Tuesdays and Fridays between 2 and 6 pm and is free within 8 km, so her condo is well within range. For the first packs this Saturday, we can either hold them for you to pick up or my colleague Joel can drop them off before 1 pm. Please let me know which you prefer.

3. We arrange the transfer for you. We call her current pharmacy directly, so there is nothing for her to sign. We only need the name and address of that pharmacy and her OHIP number. You can reply to this email or call me with those.

4. I would be happy to go over her medication list with you. First, though, we need your mother's permission, because her health information is hers and we cannot discuss it with anyone else, including family, without her consent. We record this on a short Family Communication Consent form, which she signs once. It is there to protect her privacy, and once it is on file I can speak with you freely. She can sign it when the packs are picked up, or we can send it with the driver.

I would also like to offer a MedsCheck, which is a medication review we do after a hospital discharge. It takes about 20 minutes, and since your mother may not be very mobile, I can do it at her home. I could come on Monday, November 16 or Tuesday, November 17, after 6 pm. If you are able to be there, the three of us can go through everything together in person, which may be easier for her than the phone.

There are two things I need to ask of you before Thursday.

First, please ask the discharge team to fax her prescriptions to us early Thursday morning. We need about 48 hours to prepare the first packs once we have all of her prescriptions, both the new ones from the hospital and those transferred from her current pharmacy. If the fax arrives Thursday morning, the packs will be ready on Saturday.

Second, this means the packs will not be ready when she leaves the hospital. Please confirm with the discharge team that she will go home with enough medication to last until Saturday, and that someone will be able to help her with every dose until the packs arrive. Given that she has been mixing up her pills, I would not want her managing the new ones alone for those first two days.

My direct line is 905-555-0148, extension 2. I am in the store Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm, and you are welcome to call me with any questions.

We look forward to taking care of your mother.

Sincerely,

Rania Haddad
Pharmacist
Erindale Park Pharmacy
